q: Inertial manifolds for dissipative PDEs are finite-dimensional invariant manifolds that:
opts: Attract all solutions exponentially and contain the global attractor
Are spanned by unstable modes only
Have the same dimension as the phase space
exp: An inertial manifold M is finite-dimensional, invariant, and exponentially attracting: every solution approaches M at exponential rate. The global attractor lies in M, yielding a finite-dimensional ODE (the inertial form) governing long-time behavior.
